item.title: What 42 massive and decaying presidential heads say about America
item.description: “America is really, really good at getting things very, very wrong,” mused 41-year-old Treloar Price, a clinical psychologist, “and then working hard to try to fix it.”

item.title: College baseball notebook: Spartans open on high note with top-10 series win against Louisville
item.description: Michigan State’s 142-year-old baseball program is known more for producing individual talents like Steve Garvey, Kirk Gibson and Hall of Fame pitcher Robin Roberts than for winning a lot of games. So the Spartans had reason to celebrate the opening weekend of the season, even though it didn’t end the way they would have liked.

item.title: Frankel makes 21 saves, US beats Sweden 5-0 to reach Olympic women’s hockey final
item.description: Aerin Frankel stopped 21 shots for her third shutout of the Olympic women’s hockey tournament and the favored United States advanced to the gold-medal game by defeating Sweden 5-0 at the Milan Cortina Games on Monday.

item.title: Trying to tame the Olympic controversy, World Curling sent in the umps. Then it sent them away
item.description: Curlers say they take pride in officiating themselves.

item.title: Trump administration ordered to restore George Washington slavery exhibit it removed in Philadelphia
item.description: The order came on Presidents Day, the federal holiday honoring Washington’s legacy.

item.title: Former Michigan RB lands Big Ten job after resigning as Wayne State head coach
item.description: Tyrone Wheatley is headed back to the Big Ten. The former Michigan star running back was named Illinois’ running back coach on Monday – six days after he resigned as Wayne State’s head football coach.

item.description: Towards the end of last season, Novi head coach Chris Housey told his team after a loss to Canton, “We still control our own destiny.”
